newsitem.title: USA: Playpen firm to provide repair kits after toddler's death.
newsitem.headline: Playpen firm to provide repair kits after toddler's death.

text.p: A playpen manufacturer recently blamed for a Virginia toddler's death will provide free repair kits for two of its collapsable models, the Consumer Product Safety Commission said on Thursday.
Century Products Company of Macedonia, Ohio, is voluntarily providing the kits for about 212,000 Century Fold-N-Go Model 10-710 and 10-810 Travel Playards, the CPSC reported.

An 18-month-old Manassas, Virginia, boy died in October after a Century "playard" collapsed on him at a day care site. Police said it appeared that parts of the playpen had fallen onto the boy's neck, choking him to death.
"The top rails on these playards may collapse unexpectedly, trapping a child at the neck," the CPSC said in a news release.
The playpen in the October incident and the other model for which the repair kit is being provided are built to fold compactly and to fit in a nylon case for storing and carrying.
The repair kits consist of top rails to prevent the beams from collapsing while children are in the playpens.
Owners of either model should call Century at 800-541-0264 to receive a repair kit.
